summary: Panel-by-panel reference for the Niagara System/Emitter editor: menus, toolbar (Compile, Bounds, Performance, Debug, Simulation, Baker), Preview viewport options, Parameters, System Overview, Scratch Pad, Selection stack color coding, Timeline, Curves, Niagara Log, Attribute Spreadsheet and Generated Code panels.
gotchas: Attribute Spreadsheet debugging of in-level systems requires setting the system to Force Solo and running PIE
Attribute debugger is for CPU VM-based effects
Custom modules/dynamic inputs may be hidden until Library Only is unchecked
GPU Profiling can be expensive for simulation stages with many iterations

summary: Hub for the Niagara module reference: explains stack execution order (System, Emitter, Particle, Render groups), the difference between modules and items, and the four execution states for systems and emitters.

Reference for Niagara Event Handlers: Event Handler Properties (Source, Execution Mode, Max Events Per Frame, spawn counts) and the Receive Collision/Death/Location Event items used to make one emitter react to another's events.
gotchas: Events only work with CPU simulations, not GPU
The generating emitter must have Requires Persistent IDs enabled in Emitter Properties
Execution Mode Every Particle can cause a large amount of runtime work
Events beyond Max Events Per Frame are ignored

summary: Lists the Emitter Properties item settings: Local Space, Determinism and Random Seed, Sim Target (CPU/GPU), Fixed Bounds, Interpolated Spawning, Requires Persistent ID, per-quality-level scalability platform filters, and asset/library options.
gotchas: Interpolated Spawning adds significant spawn cost
Determinism only holds when delta time is not variable
Consoles and some mobile platforms are not listed in scalability unless configured with device profiles

summary: Reference for Emitter Spawn group modules (run once when the emitter is created): Spawn Particles in Grid, Spawn Rate, Spawn Per Unit, Vertex Animation Tool morph target modules, plus the Set Parameter options listing Emitter.* parameters and data interface/primitive types you can create.
gotchas: Occlusion Query data interface only works with GPU emitters
Simple Counter data interface only works with CPU emitters
Scratch Pad items made via the Window menu must be added to the script manually

summary: Reference for Emitter Update group modules (run each emitter tick): Beam Emitter Setup, Spawn from Chaos, Emitter State (Life Cycle Mode, Inactive Response, looping, distance/visibility culling), spawning modules (Spawn Burst Instantaneous, Spawn Per Frame, Spawn Rate, Spawn Per Unit), Emitter Frame Counter, and Set Parameter options.
gotchas: Life Cycle Mode System is generally more optimal than Self
Occlusion Query is GPU-only; Simple Counter is CPU-only

summary: Full catalogue of Particle Spawn modules (run once per new particle): Initialize Particle/Ribbon, location shapes, forces, velocity, mesh sampling, orientation, SubUV, texture sampling, Dynamic Material Parameters, beams, kill modules, plus every Particles.* attribute settable via Set Parameter.
gotchas: Sample Texture module is GPU-simulation only
Kill Particles in Volume in Particle Update needs Interpolated Spawn or particles live one frame
Point Force/Add Velocity from Point should sit after location modules or they inject random velocity
Custom sprite alignment/facing modules need Sprite Renderer set to Custom Alignment/Custom Facing Vector with mask 1,1,1

summary: Full catalogue of Particle Update modules (run per particle each frame): Collision, color scaling, constraints/pendulum, Generate Collision/Death/Location Event, forces, Particle State lifetime, size scaling, Sprite Rotation Rate, Update Beam, ribbon width, velocity modules, plus settable Particles.* attributes.
gotchas: Collision module must be placed immediately before the solver module
GPU collision uses scene depth or global distance field; CPU uses raycasts
Kill Particles in Volume requires Interpolated Spawn enabled
Pendulum Constraint requires the Pendulum Setup module

summary: Reference for a Niagara system's System Settings group: User Parameters (set from Blueprint/C++) and System Properties such as Effect Type, Scalability Overrides, Fixed Bounds, Auto Deactivate, Max Pool Size, warmup settings and Bake Out Rapid Iteration.
gotchas: User Parameters can only be set from outside the simulation (Blueprint or C++)
Warmup Time/Tick Count can cause hitches
Bake Out Rapid Iteration improves performance but makes iteration much harder
Dump Debug options log every frame and are very verbose

summary: Reference for System Spawn group modules (run once when a system is created): Spawn Burst Instantaneous for all emitters, Scratch Pad modules, and Set Parameter options for System.* parameters and creatable data interface/primitive types.
gotchas: Occlusion Query is GPU-only; Simple Counter is CPU-only

summary: Reference for System Update group modules (run per system each frame): the System State module (Inactive Response, Loop Behavior, Loop Duration, Recalculate Duration Each Loop, Loop Delay) and Set Parameter options for System.* parameters.

Step-by-step lightning beam from the Static Beam template using Ribbon Renderer, Beam Emitter Setup, Spawn Beam, Beam Width, Update Beam and Jitter Position, then binding the beam end to a level actor via a Scratch Pad dynamic input and a User Parameter.
gotchas: Update Beam must sit above Jitter Position for jitter to work
Scratch Pad changes must be applied with Apply to propagate to the system
Jitter Delay set negative (-.01) to remove the underlying arc

summary: Tutorial that duplicates the FX_Smoke sprite emitter, creates a system from it, and tweaks lifetime, random color, sprite size, velocity, Acceleration Force and a Pulse alpha curve to make darker smoke.
gotchas: Requires Starter Content and the FX_Smoke emitter from the Sprite Smoke tutorial

summary: Tutorial switching a Simple Sprite Burst emitter to GPU simulation to spawn thousands of sprites, then shaping it with Sphere Location, Scale Sprite Size curves, Curl Noise Force, Point Attraction Force and a Color from Curve gradient.
gotchas: GPU simulation needs Fixed Bounds set because the system cannot read the effect's size

summary: Tutorial replacing a sprite renderer with a Ribbon Renderer and using Shape Location (Ring/Disk), Add Velocity From Point and Acceleration Force to make a falling spiral ribbon.
gotchas: DefaultRibbonMaterial only appears in the picker after enabling Show Engine Content and Show Plugin Content
No ribbon is visible until Particle Spawn settings are configured

summary: Base sprite smoke tutorial: set Sprite Renderer to a SubUV material (8x8), use Spawn Rate, randomized lifetime/size/rotation, Add Velocity, Shape Location, SubUV Animation and Acceleration Force, then save the emitter as a reusable asset.
gotchas: Requires Starter Content for M_smoke_subUV
Without SubUV Animation the renderer only shows the first frame of the sprite sheet

summary: Multi-emitter tutorial building a sparks system from three emitters (smoke, central spark burst, radial velocity-aligned sparks) with Gravity Force, Drag, Collision bounce/friction and Scale Sprite Size by Speed.
keys: Calculate Size and Rotational Inertia by Mass
gotchas: Requires Starter Content materials and the FX_Smoke emitter from the Sprite Smoke tutorial

summary: Tutorial duplicating FX_Smoke into a steam emitter, adjusting spawn rate, lifetime, sprite size, velocity and acceleration ranges, a Pulse Out alpha curve, and adding Drag.
gotchas: New modules are added to the bottom of the stack; Drag after Solve Forces and Velocity triggers an unmet dependencies error fixed with Fix Issue
Requires Starter Content and the FX_Smoke emitter

summary: Compares four ways to play sound from Niagara: Play Audio module (one-shot, cheapest), Play Persistent Audio with Update Persistent Audio (updatable), the Audio Component Renderer, and exporting particle data to Blueprint/C++, with pros and cons of each.
gotchas: Audio Component Renderer is experimental and not recommended except for special cases
Play Audio sounds cannot be changed or stopped once triggered and do not follow particles
Persistent audio modules must share the same audio player reference created in emitter/system spawn
Export Particle Data is slowest; works on GPU emitters with added latency

summary: Tutorial building a glowing fountain from the Fountain template, using emissive color values above 1, Collision, and a Light Renderer with Radius Scale and Color Add so particles light the scene.
gotchas: Collision added after Solve Forces and Velocity errors until Fix Issue moves it
Color values greater than 1 become emissive

summary: Shows how to confirm or enable the Niagara plugin under Edit > Plugins > FX and restart, after which the Content Browser right-click menu gains the FX section.
gotchas: Niagara is enabled by default in UE5; enabling it requires an editor restart

summary: Tutorial making mesh particles: build a material driven by Particle Color, swap the Fountain template's Sprite Renderer for a Mesh Renderer with Override Materials, and randomize mesh scale, color and velocity for rising balloons.
gotchas: Material must use a Particle Color node for Niagara color to apply
Sprite attributes should be set to Unset when using mesh particles

summary: Hub for a tutorial series on using Niagara with Sequencer for linear/cinematic output: rendering, controlling systems, display rate, caching and reuse, pre-roll warmup, motion blur and production considerations.
Top-level Niagara hub linking to Getting Started, Tutorials, Niagara Fluids, Collisions, custom modules, Lightweight Emitters, Debugging and Optimization, and the Reference section.
gotchas: GPU Raytracing Collisions module is experimental
